comment: Status of every js_facade_gen reference case (def_files/js_facade_gen_test_cases.md) under test/conformance/normalize.ts. parity: normalized output is identical. improved: dartify deliberately emits something more precise or more correct, stated in the note. differs: a known, accepted difference. outOfScope: not expressible as a single .d.ts snippet or not declaration syntax. Cases not listed must be at parity. `pnpm test` fails if a parity case regresses or a non-parity case starts matching (promote it).

2.14.note: Constructor parameter properties are implementation syntax; declaration files spell them as separate properties, which are covered by 2.6/2.13.

2.16.note: Promise<T> is a typed interop class with a toFuture() extension instead of a hand-written private shadow class per method; await foo().toFuture().

2.17.note: Real Dart generic methods (Z<T>()) instead of dynamic /*T*/ comments (E-03).

2.18.note: Each overload keeps its exact signature as F_1/F_2/F_3 bound to JavaScript F through @JS extension members, instead of one merged dynamic signature.

3.9.note: An invalid JavaScript property name is bound through a renamed extension member with an exact, escaped @JS name instead of being commented out.

4.1.note: The interface+var merge is a concrete class with an external generative constructor, so it can also be extended; js_facade_gen emits an abstract class with a factory.

4.2.note: js_facade_gen's expected output declares static and instance members both named b, which is a Dart compile error; dartify binds the static as a top-level X_b_2 getter/setter.

4.3.note: The merge carries static members, so it is bound @JS("X") rather than @anonymous, which could not reach X.d at runtime.

5.1.note: Namespace members are flattened into the library (with collision-safe names), so the qualified reference foo.Bar resolves to the emitted class Bar.

5.4.note: An inline object type becomes a real @anonymous class with a factory instead of dynamic /*{x: string, y: number}*/.

5.5.note: An index-signature object becomes a class with typed operator []/[]= instead of dynamic /*JSMap of ...*/ (E-14).

5.14.note: f keeps its type parameter K; keyof/indexed access degrade to the named typedefs KeyOfA/IndexedAK instead of inline dynamic comments (E-16).

6.7.note: Real generics: List<T> sort<T, U>(List<T> xs) instead of dynamic /*T*/ comments (E-03).

7.1.note: Enums are abstract classes: a runtime enum object has no JavaScript constructor, so Dart must not allow Color() (E-35).

8.1.note: Needs the module 'y' as a second input; import-equals of an absent module has no package:js meaning.

8.2.note: Needs module 'X' as a second input. Star re-exports become export directives (with ambiguity hides) in multi-file runs; covered by test/decl/decl-emitter.test.ts and three.js.

8.3.note: Needs module 'X' as a second input. Named re-exports become export ... show directives in multi-file runs.

8.5.note: The third colliding top-level x is x_2, dartify's single collision-suffix style (E-29/E-30), where js_facade_gen used x2.

9.1.note: The author's alias stays a named typedef (typedef MyNumber = num) instead of being inlined and commented out.

11.4.note: A documentation block with no declaration has nothing to attach to.

12.1.note: The destructured parameter has a TypeScript default, so it is optional ([dynamic p_d]); js_facade_gen made it required Object.
